title: hello-channel-telegram — a bot that lives in a chat (target: channel)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: A long-running daemon that runs one model turn per inbound Telegram message. It's webhook-served — beat 3 registers the URL.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the tokens
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the bot token and the API key for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: an agent with a phone number

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines. channel isn't a REPL — it's a daemon that waits for other people to talk.”

beats.label: Add the agent
beats.cue: “Reply concisely — 1 to 2 sentences.” The same agent block every other target uses.

beats.label: Give it one tool
beats.cue: “Ground answers in repo state” — read, and nothing else. A chat bot with a filesystem.

beats.label: Wire Telegram
beats.cue: Both tokens are env references, never literals — this spec is safe to commit.

beats.label: Decide what a conversation is
beats.cue: sessionKey: thread — one session per chat thread, so two chats never share memory.

beats.label: Scope it before it's unattended
beats.cue: An unattended daemon can't stop to ask you — so what it may do is declared up front.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Look at botToken: kind env, name TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. The secret never enters the artifact.”

verify.note: prints the 46-line IR for target channel — channels.telegram tokens lower to {kind:"env"} refs

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no bot token.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the spec env refs gate

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “Adapter, gateway, session router, janitor, SIGTERM handler — from twenty lines of YAML.”

beats.label: Find the boot gate
beats.cue: “It names the exact variables it needs, then exits 2 — before it makes a single API call.”

verify.note: 6 matching lines (21, 23, 25, 26, 31, 32) — the required-env gate lowered from the spec's env refs, ending in process.exit(2)

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A channel is a daemon — the CLI names the shapes it takes.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "channel")`

beats.label: Boot the daemon with no secrets
beats.cue: “There's the gate, live: it names every var it needs before it opens a socket — and exits 2.”
beats.command: env -u TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN -u TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY bun live/dist/daemon.ts

verify.note: designed refusal — `[daemon] missing required env vars: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; env -u scrubs what Setup sourced, so the gate fires either way

beats.label: Give the webhook a public URL
beats.cue: [manual] Telegram only POSTs to a public HTTPS host — ngrok lends localhost:3000 one.

verify.note: needs ngrok (or any tunnel) installed and a second terminal; the emitted daemon is webhook-only — there is no polling path

beats.label: Keep the tunnel host
beats.cue: [manual] Paste the https host ngrok just printed — the next beat registers exactly this.

verify.note: the operator substitutes their own tunnel host; the export persists in the demo terminal for the provision beat

beats.label: Point Telegram at your daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] setWebhook, for real: your bot now POSTs updates to $TUNNEL_URL/telegram/events.

verify.note: live setWebhook — needs TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN and a tunnel host the operator owns; changes remote state on the operator's own bot

beats.label: Boot the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Two tokens and an API key: it's listening on :3000 for /telegram/events.”

verify.note: needs TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN + Anthropic credentials; serves the gateway on PORT (default 3000)

beats.label: Find the conversation on disk
beats.cue: [manual] DM the bot, then ⌃C the daemon: one session transcript per chat thread.

verify.note: needs a human to DM the bot from Telegram and stop the daemon; the transcript only exists after a real keyed turn through the registered webhook

groups.title: One more thing · what that setWebhook call was

beats.label: Print the call instead of sending it
beats.cue: “Same command, --dry-run: the exact POST — url, secret token, allowed_updates. Secrets redacted.”
beats.command: crewhaus channel provision live/crewhaus.yaml --platform telegram --base-url https://bot.example.com --dry-run

verify.note: prints the POST to api.telegram.org/bot$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/setWebhook with url https://bot.example.com/telegram/events; sends nothing

beats.label: Where the path comes from
beats.cue: “The gateway routes /<adapter>/events. daemon.ts registers this one as telegram — that's the whole URL.”

verify.note: 4 lines — gateway.ts:90-91 match /^\/([^/]+)\/events$/, daemon.ts:44,88 bind the name "telegram" to the adapter

beats.label: Run the scope doctor — dry
beats.cue: “verify asks Telegram whether it agrees with your spec: getWebhookInfo, printed not sent.”

verify.note: prints the getWebhookInfo GET it would make; no network

beats.label: Ask Telegram for real
beats.cue: [needs-key] Live getWebhookInfo against the URL you just registered — exit 1 the moment it drifts.

verify.note: read-only — GETs api.telegram.org with $TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; --base-url upgrades the webhook-URL checks from ~ to ✓/✗; exits 1 on a hard failure
